name: BranchDeck
tagline: Your local AI projects, branches, and shortcut commands
description: Bring local Codex and Claude Code projects into one macOS workspace. Group related Git worktrees, find each branch checkout, and keep test, build, and dev shortcuts with its directory. Select a workspace to see its commands and terminal output. Local discovery; no BranchDeck account. Free preview for Apple Silicon Macs, with a Chinese interface. Gallery: real app screenshots using fictional projects.
status: Successfully scheduled on Product Hunt for 2026-10-11 at 00:01 America/Los_Angeles (15:01 Asia/Shanghai).
makerComment: I built BranchDeck to organize the local project directories left across Codex, Claude Code, and parallel Git worktrees. The core is simple: project → branch checkout → useful commands. Find a repository, select its local branch workspace, and keep test, build, or dev shortcuts beside that directory. Commands belong to workspace directories; they do not automatically follow a branch name when you check out something else. The gallery shows the real app with fictional projects. This free preview is for Apple Silicon Macs and currently has a Chinese interface. Which part of managing your local AI projects and branch commands would you improve first?
